lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Renato | Lesson 29 -- Anything Might Happen
lesson.grammar_point: might and may for possibility (might / may / might not / may not + base verb)

listenings.text: Okay, Renato, a quick update before your quarterfinal. The conditions this afternoon are unpredictable. The tide is higher now, so the peak might move closer to the beach. The wind is changing too. There may be some strong gusts from the south, and they might make the waves choppy. Your opponents are Finn Carter, Ethan Moss and Noah Brooks. Finn is a local, and he won this contest last year, so everybody thinks you're the underdog. That's fine. No pressure. There might be a long lull in the middle of the heat, so don't panic if the ocean goes flat. And if you're not in the lead after ten minutes, there's still time for a comeback. I'm not certain about the scores today, but two good sixes may be enough. Okay? Breathe. You're ready.

Jess, it's Kai. You're missing it! Renato's quarterfinal started ten minutes ago, and it's crazy. Finn got a seven on his first wave, so he's in the lead. Then there was a long lull, nothing for five minutes. Renato just sat there on his board, really calm. And then a big set came, and he didn't hesitate. He got a great wave, maybe a seven too. Now he might be in second place, but I'm not certain. Ethan Moss is really close. There are four minutes left, and the wind is changing again, so the last waves might be messy. He may need one more good wave. Honestly, anything might happen. The scores might be on the board in a minute. I'll call you after the horn. Okay, bye!

items.situation: Jess asks: "Are you going to win the quarterfinal?" You're not sure. Answer her.
Tom wants to paddle out now. Look at the sky and the ocean. Tell him what might happen.
Your opponent Finn is in the lead after five minutes. Say what you might still do.
Dave asks if he can come to the beach tomorrow. Tell him what you might do, and what you might not do.
Your teacher asks about your weekend. You have no plans yet. Give two possibilities.
